It was the Mogo program, which scored this first victory in an exhibition game played during the US Go Congress.[[147]](#cite_note-161)[[148]](#cite_note-162) By 2013, a win at the professional level of play was accomplished with a four-stone advantage.[[149]](#cite_note-163)[[150]](#cite_note-164) In October 2015, [Google DeepMind](/wiki/Google_DeepMind "Google DeepMind")'s program [AlphaGo](/wiki/AlphaGo "AlphaGo") beat [Fan Hui](/wiki/Fan_Hui "Fan Hui"), the European Go champion and a [2 dan](/wiki/Go_ranks_and_ratings "Go ranks and ratings") (out of 9 dan possible) professional, [five times out of five](/wiki/AlphaGo_versus_Fan_Hui "AlphaGo versus Fan Hui") with no handicap on a full size 19×19 board.[[137]](#cite_note-AlphaGo-150) AlphaGo used a fundamentally different paradigm than earlier Go programs; it included very little direct instruction, and mostly used [deep learning](/wiki/Deep_learning "Deep learning") where AlphaGo played itself in hundreds of millions of games such that it could measure positions more intuitively. In March 2016, Google next challenged [Lee Sedol](/wiki/Lee_Sedol "Lee Sedol"), a 9 dan considered the top player in the world in the early 21st century,[[151]](#cite_note-165) to a [five-game match](/wiki/AlphaGo_versus_Lee_Sedol "AlphaGo versus Lee Sedol"). The University of Michigan's campus in Ann Arbor is divided into four main areas: the Central Campus area, the North Campus area, the North Medical Campus area, and Ross Athletic Campus area. The campus areas include more than 500 major buildings, with a combined area of more than 37.48 million square feet (860 acres; 3.482 km2). The Central and Athletic Campus areas are contiguous, while the North Campus area is separated from them, primarily by the [Huron River](/wiki/Huron_River_(Michigan) "Huron River (Michigan)"). The North Medical Campus area was developed on Plymouth Road, with several university-owned buildings for outpatient care, diagnostics, and outpatient surgery.[[115]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMacInnes1979-131)

There is leased space in buildings scattered throughout the city, many occupied by organizations affiliated with the University of Michigan Health System. In addition to the University of Michigan Golf Course on Ross Athletic Campus, the university operates a second golf course on Geddes Road called Radrick Farms Golf Course. The Moon, Io, and Europa have compositions similar to the terrestrial planets; the others are made of ice and rock like the dwarf planets, with [Tethys](/wiki/Tethys_(moon) "Tethys (moon)") being made of almost pure ice. Europa is often considered an icy planet, though, because its surface ice layer makes it difficult to study its interior.[[4]](#cite_note-planetarysociety-4)[[36]](#cite_note-36) Ganymede and Titan are larger than Mercury by radius, and Callisto almost equals it, but all three are much less massive. Mimas is the smallest object generally agreed to be a [geophysical planet](/wiki/Geophysical_definition_of_planet "Geophysical definition of planet"), at about six millionths of Earth's mass, though there are many larger bodies that may not be geophysical planets (e.g. [Salacia](/wiki/120347_Salacia "120347 Salacia")).[[32]](#cite_note-Grundy2019-32)

The first home match for the Denmark national team was a 2–1 friendly win over England on 25 May 1910, taking place with 12,000 spectators at the stadium "KBs baner" (located in the area "Granen", where the [Forum Copenhagen](/wiki/Forum_Copenhagen "Forum Copenhagen") later was built).[[89]](#cite_note-89) As the facilities were considered too small, a new stadium in [Copenhagen](/wiki/Copenhagen "Copenhagen") was built with the name **[Idrætsparken](/wiki/K%C3%B8benhavns_Idr%C3%A6tspark "Københavns Idrætspark")**. Since its opening on 25 May 1911, it has hosted all the home matches of the football club [KB](/wiki/Kj%C3%B8benhavns_Boldklub "Kjøbenhavns Boldklub") and most of the home matches of the national team. During the first 82 years of the national team, from October 1908 until November 1990, Denmark played a total number of 254 A-level home matches, of which 232 were played in Idrætsparken. Among all the played home matches in Idrætsparken, Denmark achieved 125 victories (54%), 41 draws (18%) and 66 defeats (28%). The stadium reached a record of 51,600 spectators for the 1–2 game against Sweden in June 1957.[[90]](#cite_note-90)

In regards of the first era from 1908 to 1990, only 22 home matches were played at other stadiums than Idrætsparken, of which 11 took place at [Aarhus Idrætspark](/wiki/Aarhus_Idr%C3%A6tspark "Aarhus Idrætspark") (then known as Atletion) in [Aarhus](/wiki/Aarhus "Aarhus"), followed by [Aalborg Stadion](/wiki/Aalborg_Stadion "Aalborg Stadion") in [Aalborg](/wiki/Aalborg "Aalborg") with six games, and the remaining five matches hosted by four other stadiums. All *Narcissus* species contain the [alkaloid](/wiki/Alkaloid "Alkaloid") poison [lycorine](/wiki/Lycorine "Lycorine"), mostly in the bulb but also in the leaves.[[190]](#cite_note-Pupils_ill_after_bulb_put_in_soup-193) Members of the monocot subfamily [Amaryllidoideae](/wiki/Amaryllidoideae "Amaryllidoideae") present a unique type of alkaloids, the norbelladine alkaloids, which are [4-methylcatechol](/wiki/4-methylcatechol "4-methylcatechol") derivatives combined with [tyrosine](/wiki/Tyrosine "Tyrosine"). They are responsible for the poisonous properties of a number of the species. Over 200 different chemical structures of these compounds are known, of which 79 or more are known from *Narcissus* alone.[[191]](#cite_note-Martin-194)

The toxic effects of ingesting *Narcissus* products for both humans and animals (such as cattle, goats, pigs, and cats) have long been recognised and they have been used in suicide attempts. Ingestion of *N. pseudonarcissus* or *N. jonquilla* is followed by [salivation](/wiki/Salivation "Salivation"), acute abdominal pains, [nausea](/wiki/Nausea "Nausea"), vomiting, and [diarrhea](/wiki/Diarrhea "Diarrhea"), then neurological and cardiac events, including [trembling](/wiki/Trembling "Trembling"), [convulsions](/wiki/Convulsions "Convulsions"), and [paralysis](/wiki/Paralysis "Paralysis"). Death may result if large quantities are consumed.

The toxicity of *Narcissus* varies with species, *N. poeticus* being more toxic than *N. pseudonarcissus*, for instance.
